title: Learning What to Share: Expert Specialization for Time-Series Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2610.33822v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A central challenge in multivariate forecasting is deciding what to share across channels and where to specialize. Mixture-of-experts models offer flexible sharing, yet it remains unclear how much of their forecasting gains comes from added capacity or expert allocation. Through controlled comparisons across eleven datasets and three backbones, we show that informative channel assignments improve forecasting beyond matched shared capacity and random allocation. On frozen transformer backbones, persistent channel-specific mixtures outperform input-dependent routing on average. To examine when and how much specialization helps, we introduce GalaxyTS, a controlled synthetic dataset with exact shared and channel-specific forecasting references. It reveals how persistent channel mixtures exploit predictive differences concealed by short input windows and measures gains over matched shared corrections. These insights motivate Persistent Clos

translated_title: 学习共享什么：面向时间序列预测的专家专业化
translated_abstract: 多变量预测的一个核心挑战是决定哪些信息应在通道之间共享、在何处进行专业化。混合专家模型提供了灵活的共享机制，但其预测性能的提升究竟来自增加的容量还是专家分配方式，目前仍不清楚。通过在十一个数据集和三种主干网络上的受控比较，我们证明，有信息量的通道分配能够在匹配的共享容量和随机分配之上改进预测效果。在冻结的 Transformer 主干网络上，持久的通道特定混合平均而言优于依赖输入的路由。为了考察专业化何时以及在多大程度上有所帮助，我们引入了 GalaxyTS——一个包含精确共享与通道特定预测参考的受控合成数据集。它揭示了持久的通道混合如何利用被短输入窗口所掩盖的预测差异，并量化了相对于匹配的共享校正所带来的增益。这些见解启发了 Persistent Clos（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 论文通过受控比较证明混合专家模型在时间序列预测中的增益来自有信息量的通道分配而非单纯增加容量，持久的通道特定专家混合平均优于依赖输入的路由，并提出带精确共享与通道特定参考的合成数据集 GalaxyTS 来量化专家专业化何时以及多大程度带来收益。
en_tdlr: This paper shows through controlled comparisons that mixture-of-experts forecasting gains stem from informative channel assignments rather than added capacity, with persistent channel-specific mixtures outperforming input-dependent routing, and introduces GalaxyTS, a synthetic dataset that precisely quantifies when and how much expert specialization helps.
